text: The property lost 25.5 hectares of tree cover in 2015 due to deforestation. The evidence shows that the area was covered by trees (with at least 30% canopy density) in 2000, but by 2020, no forest cover remained in the affected area. The European Commission Joint Research Centre’s 2020 Global Forest Cover dataset confirms that the area was not forested by 2020, corroborating the loss. The University of Maryland’s Global Forest Change data specifically identifies 2015 as the year of the loss event, with no tree cover detected afterward in the affected patches. No further natural regeneration or reforestation occurred, as the area remained clear through 2025.
